record.original_question: For unrestricted Stable Marriage with Ties and Incomplete lists, close the approximability gap for finding a maximum-cardinality stable matching between the current best lower and upper bounds.

evidence.quote: These upper and lower bounds for general max smti remain the best known to date, and it is an open problem to close the gap between them.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Stable Marriage problem with Ties and Incomplete lists (SMTI). An instance consists of two disjoint finite sets, men M and women W, where each person p has a preference list that is a strict ranking of ties (equivalence classes) over a subset of the opposite side (the acceptable partners). A matching is a set of disjoint acceptable man–woman pairs. A pair (m,w), with m and w not matched to each other, is blocking for matching S if m and w find each other acceptable and each of them is either unmatched in S or strictly prefers the other to their current partner in S (ties are broken in favor of the current partner, i.e., indifference is not strict preference). A matching is stable if it admits no blocking pair. The MAX-SMTI problem asks for a stable matching of maximum cardinality.

It is known that MAX-SMTI is NP-hard and APX-hard. In the unrestricted setting (ties may appear on either or both sides, and arbitrary incomplete lists are allowed), let α* denote the infimum of constants α ≥ 1 such that there exists a polynomial-time α-approximation algorithm for MAX-SMTI, and let β* denote the supremum of constants β ≥ 1 such that MAX-SMTI cannot be approximated within β in polynomial time unless P = NP.

Determine α* exactly, and in particular close the gap between the best known polynomial-time approximation ratio (upper bound on α*) of 3/2 and the best known NP-hardness of approximation threshold (lower bound on β*) of 33/29.
artifact.status_search_result: The best known polynomial-time approximation ratio for unrestricted MAX-SMTI remains 3/2 (McDermid; Király; Paluch), and the best known inapproximability lower bound is 33/29 under P≠NP (with stronger bounds under UGC). No subsequent work has been identified that closes this gap; the problem is still considered open in the matching-under-preferences literature.

status_evidence.title: A Tight Approximation Bound for the Stable Marriage Problem with Restricted Ties
status_evidence.snippet: For general MAX SMTI the best approximation ratio is 1.5 and it cannot be approximated within 33/29 unless P=NP.
status_evidence.claim: The general MAX-SMTI gap (3/2 upper bound vs 33/29 lower bound) remains the state of the art.

status_evidence.title: Strategy-Proof Approximation Algorithms for the Stable Marriage Problem with Ties and Incomplete Lists
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses approximation status of MAX-SMTI variants, citing 1.5 as the best general ratio.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work still cites 3/2 as the best known general approximation ratio for MAX-SMTI.
